claims.quote: Preserved EF ≥50%, elevated E/e', LA enlargement, LVH HFpEF

claims.quote: Chamber sizes - LV (LVEDD, LVESD), RV (>1:1 with LV = dilated), LA, RA.

claims.quote: Wall thickness - septum, posterior wall (>11 mm = LVH).

claims.text: Doppler of mitral inflow combined with tissue Doppler imaging of the mitral annulus can help identify and quantify LV diastolic dysfunction and LV filling pressures
claims.quote: The combination of Doppler evaluation of mitral inflow with tissue Doppler imaging of the mitral annulus can help identify and quantify LV diastolic dysfunction and LV filling pressures.

claims.text: In HFpEF LV filling is impaired: increased LV end-diastolic pressure at rest or during exertion, usually a normal LV end-diastolic volume, and normal global contractility and LVEF (≥ 50%)
claims.quote: In HFpEF (also called diastolic heart failure), LV filling is impaired, resulting in: Increased LV end-diastolic pressure at rest or during exertion Usually, normal LV end-diastolic volume Global contractility and hence LV ejection fraction remain normal (≥ 50%).

claims.text: Causes Diastolic dysfunction usually results from impaired ventricular relaxation, increased ventricular stiffness, valvular disease or constrictive pericarditis; acute myocardial ischemia is also a cause
claims.quote: Diastolic dysfunction usually results from impaired ventricular relaxation (an active process), increased ventricular stiffness, valvular disease, or constrictive pericarditis. Acute myocardial ischemia is also a cause of diastolic dysfunction.

claims.text: Particularly common among older adults (resistance to filling increases with age); predominates in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, other disorders with ventricular hypertrophy (eg, hypertension, significant aortic stenosis) and amyloid infiltration of the myocardium
claims.quote: Resistance to filling increases with age, reflecting cardiomyocyte dysfunction and cardiomyocyte loss, and increased interstitial collagen deposition; thus, diastolic dysfunction is particularly common among older adults. Diastolic dysfunction predominates in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, other disorders with ventricular hypertrophy (eg, hypertension, significant aortic stenosis), and amyloid infiltration of the myocardium.

claims.text: Approximately 50% of patients with heart failure have HFpEF, more with age and diabetes; data suggest comorbidities (eg, obesity, hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease) lead to systemic inflammation, endothelial and cardiac microvascular dysfunction and, ultimately, molecular changes that cause increased myocardial fibrosis and ventricular stiffening
claims.quote: Approximately 50% of patients with heart failure have HFpEF; the prevalence increases with age and in patients with diabetes (3). HFpEF is a complex, heterogenous, multiorgan, systemic syndrome, often with multiple concomitant pathophysiologies. Data suggest that multiple comorbidities (eg, obesity, hypertension, diabetes, chronic kidney disease) lead to systemic inflammation, widespread endothelial dysfunction, cardiac microvascular dysfunction, and, ultimately, molecular changes in the heart that cause increased myocardial fibrosis and ventricular stiffening.

claims.text: Symptoms Elevated left atrial pressures can cause pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary congestion; in some patients marked restriction to LV filling can cause low cardiac output and systemic symptoms
claims.quote: However, in some patients, marked restriction to LV filling can cause inappropriately low LV end-diastolic volume and thus cause low cardiac output and systemic symptoms. Elevated left atrial pressures can cause pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary congestion.

claims.text: LV failure: the most common symptoms are dyspnea and fatigue; dyspnea may be exertional or occur at rest, depending on severity
claims.quote: In LV failure, the most common symptoms are dyspnea and fatigue due to increased pulmonary venous pressures with or without pulmonary edema, and low cardiac output (at rest or inability to augment cardiac output during exertion). Dyspnea may be exertional or occur with rest, depending on the severity of disease.

claims.text: S3 and S4 and an accentuated P2 can also occur in HFpEF
claims.quote: Audible and occasionally palpable third (S3) and fourth (S4) heart sounds Accentuated pulmonic component (P2) of the second heart sound (S2) These abnormal heart sounds also can occur in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or heart failure with minimally reduced ejection fraction (HRmrEF).

claims.text: Pulmonary findings: early inspiratory basilar crackles that do not clear with coughing; with a pleural effusion, dullness to percussion and diminished breath sounds at the base(s)
claims.quote: Pulmonary findings include early inspiratory basilar crackles that do not clear with coughing and, if pleural effusion is present, dullness to percussion and diminished breath sounds at the lung base(s).

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: diuresis, treat HTN, SGLT2i

Recommended for HFpEF: an SGLT2 inhibitor for all patients, diuretics for congestion and symptoms, and mineralocorticoid antagonists and angiotensin-renin system inhibition for select patient groups; treat hypertension, atherosclerotic disease and atrial fibrillation
claims.quote: Recommended therapies for HFpEF include an SGLT2 inhibitor for all patients, diuretics for patients with congestion and symptoms, and mineralocorticoid antagonists and angiotensin-renin system inhibition for select patient groups (1, 2, 13). Cardiovascular comorbidities, including hypertension, atherosclerotic disease, and atrial fibrillation should be treated.
claims.locator: Medical therapy of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

claims.text: SGLT2 inhibitors (eg, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) have shown significant survival benefit in heart failure regardless of ejection fraction
claims.quote: SGLT2 inhibitors (eg, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) have demonstrated significant survival benefit for patients with heart failure, regardless of ejection fraction (1, 2, 9, 10).

claims.text: Formal exercise through cardiac rehabilitation is likely helpful in chronic HFpEF
claims.quote: Formal exercise through cardiac rehabilitation is useful for patients with chronic HFrEF and is likely helpful for patients with chronic HFpEF.
